questions.text: Is the blood in your urine visible to the naked eye (frank haematuria), and when during urination does it appear — at the start, throughout, or at the end?
questions.purpose: Characterise haematuria type and timing; painless frank haematuria throughout urination is the classic bladder cancer presentation
options: Visible blood — at start of urination (initial)
Visible blood — at end of urination (terminal)
Blood only detected on urine dipstick (microscopic)

questions.text: Is the haematuria painless — that is, there is no burning, stinging, or pain when you pass urine?
questions.purpose: Painless haematuria is the classic red flag presentation of bladder or kidney malignancy

questions.text: Are you over 45 years of age and a current or ex-smoker?
questions.purpose: Age >45 with smoking is a high-risk combination for urothelial malignancy in the context of haematuria

questions.text: Do you have any flank pain, a palpable abdominal mass, or unexplained weight loss?
questions.purpose: Flank pain and mass in the context of haematuria suggest renal cell carcinoma (classic triad)

questions.text: Do you have any symptoms of urinary tract infection — burning, frequency, urgency, or fever?
questions.purpose: Identify UTI as a common benign cause of haematuria; note that UTI does not fully exclude malignancy in high-risk patients

questions.text: Have you had any occupational exposure to chemicals such as aniline dyes, benzene, or aromatic amines?
questions.purpose: Occupational chemical exposure is a known risk factor for urothelial malignancy

questions.text: Have you had previous bladder tumours, kidney stones, or urological procedures?
questions.purpose: History of prior bladder cancer is the strongest risk factor for recurrence
